purpose: Which of the records that carry a development figure and an adopted gross written premium at or below zero are in run-off in that year, by their own filings (the author's decision D1, option A as refined, 30 September 2026). A premium sign is not a run-off test: 3623/2018 is a live syndicate whose negative premium is a return premium under a reinsurance contract, and 5183/2024's filing puts its run-off at 1 January 2025. in_runoff is true only where the filing states that the syndicate itself is in run-off, has ceased underwriting or is being wound down during that year; a run-off year of account, and the reinsurance to close of closed years, are not that. Where the filing's standard going concern wording says the syndicate will continue to write business and the same filing states that the syndicate is in run-off, the run-off statement decides, on the author's reading, and the going concern wording is recorded verbatim in the note (2255/2015). A statement that is ambiguous leaves the record where it is (in_runoff false) and the note says why.
premium_adopted_gbp_m: the adopted gross written premium as the record states it, in millions of the currency in premium_currency (the extraction's convention for every _gbp_m field); both models' readings agree for all nine

records.note: In run-off, on the author's reading of this filing's own account (30 September 2026). Its Future developments statement (the evidence; pdf page 10, printed 6) says the syndicate 'continues to run-off its portfolio of liabilities' and that the 2013 year of account was reinsured to close into 2015 'for administrative purposes only'. The filing names a Syndicate Run-off Manager (pdf page 6, printed 2), says no RITC contracts of Lloyd's syndicates were underwritten in 2015 (pdf page 7, printed 3) and prints a gross premium written of (362) thousand pounds, the negative premium the record adopted (pdf page 16, printed 12); all three fit that account. Four passages could be read the other way and are recorded so that a reader sees all of them. The going concern paragraph (pdf page 21, printed 17) is the standard going concern statement of the basis of preparation and is not read as saying that the syndicate underwrites new business; it reads, verbatim: 'Having taken into account the risks and uncertainties and the performance of the syndicate as disclosed in the Report of the directors and making inquiries, the managing agent has a reasonable expectation that the syndicate will continue to write business for the foreseeable future. Moreover, the managing agent expects that continued capital support will be in place in order to do so. Accordingly, the financial statements have been prepared on the going concern basis.' The Statement of Managing Agent's Responsibilities (pdf page 13, printed 9) says the accounts are prepared on the basis that the syndicate 'will continue to write future business unless it is inappropriate to presume the syndicate will do so'. The Future developments paragraph itself ends 'Syndicate 2255 will continue to search for and evaluate suitable new business propositions.' and the income statement ends 'All operations are continuing.' (pdf page 16, printed 12). The syndicate is a reinsurance-to-close vehicle: it commenced underwriting on 1 January 2011 and was set up to underwrite the RITC of Lloyd's syndicates (pdf page 7, printed 3), and in 2011 it wrote the RITC of Syndicate 1861 (2008 and prior) and of Syndicate 340 (1998 to 2001) (pdf page 8, printed 4).
